correctness.rationale: The distinctness, degree and count assertions are correct. Kyselov Proposition 4.1 permits p=73 (4 divides 72) and imposes no nonvanishing condition at index 2; all indices used are below h=18. Independently expanding the logarithm with its alternating power series gives coefficients (18,0,49,25,52,56) at indices 1 through 6 modulo 73. Equal first and third power traces recover the norm via Tr(x^3)=u^3-3uN when the common trace u is nonzero. On the nonzero trace-zero line, the fourth and sixth traces determine the scalar modulo sign, and sign is Frobenius there. Inversion commutes with Frobenius; Frobenius substitution gives the reverse implication. Theorem 1.1 covers the remaining primes since D_4=-3650. Scaling variables by a^{-1} gives the stated cyclotomic action. The scalar conjugacies in the base field are only 1 for nonzero trace, and plus or minus 1 for zero trace (a scalar relating b to b^p must square to 1). Counting fourth-power preimages gives the degree formulas. The 72 fixed and 2628 two-element orbits at p=73 give 2700. The 'genuinely new' framing fails originality, not these mathematical assertions.
residual_risks: The direct replay is for p=73 only. It compares integer trace histograms modulo the constant histogram (the relation Phi_73), not floating-point values; all other primes use the stated theorem. The proof does not rederive the cited p-adic results.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The two prior theorems together cover every prime in the frozen range; exclusion from the first criterion is not exclusion from the stronger test.
